verdict.rationale: Statsig ships an official MCP server that lets users of AI clients such as Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code "ask questions, explore experiments, and access your Statsig data using AI." That is first-party natural-language access to the product. The documented scope is querying and exploring data, not issuing commands that create or change gates and experiments. The natural-language path also runs only through external AI clients, with no built-in assistant. missing for 10: documented natural-language write/operate actions (creating or toggling gates, launching experiments), an in-product natural-language interface, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: With this setup, you can ask questions, explore experiments, and access your Statsig data using AI.
The Statsig MCP (Model Context Protocol) server brings the power of Statsig into tools like Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code.
